title: Developing a Named Entity Recognition Dataset for Tagalog
venue: Proceedings of the First Workshop for Southeast Asian Language Processing (SEALP 2023) at IJCNLP-AACL 2023
problem_statement: How to overcome the scarcity of high-quality Named Entity Recognition (NER) resources for Tagalog (a low-resource Philippine language) by curating a publicly accessible, gold-standard annotated corpus from modern news reports and establishing empirical baselines across supervised, transfer learning, and zero-shot large language model configurations.
domain: Natural Language Processing (NLP), Named Entity Recognition (NER), Low-Resource Languages, Philippine Languages (Tagalog / Filipino), News Domain
theoretical_framework: Transition-based dependency and entity span parsing using the BILUO sequence encoding scheme and maxout convolutional neural networks (Honnibal et al., 2020); token-level and boundary-level information-theoretic distinctiveness metrics based on Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence of unigram distributions (Papay et al., 2020); and monolingual/multilingual contextual representation transfer (Cruz and Cheng, 2022; Conneau et al., 2020; Devlin et al., 2019).
methodology: A dataset curation, annotation, and benchmarking framework comprising: (1) Corpus curation: Extracting and filtering news texts from the TLUnified pretraining corpus spanning 2009 to early 2020 across politics, weather, and science; (2) Iterative annotation: Using Prodigy with the ner.manual recipe across six rounds (18 weeks total) with three native Tagalog speakers annotating three CoNLL-style entity categories (Person, Organization, Location; excluding MISC), conducting retrospective guideline calibration after each round; (3) Annotation evaluation: Measuring inter-annotator agreement via two Cohen's kappa formulations (token-level non-null kappa = 0.81, non-O kappa = 0.83) and reference F1 (0.89), alongside Span Distinctiveness (SD) and Boundary Distinctiveness (BD) metrics; (4) Supervised modeling: Training spaCy transition-based parsers with BILUO encoding and maxout CNNs using four embedding configurations: from scratch (baseline), static Tagalog fastText vectors with UTF-8 byte cloze pretraining, fine-tuned monolingual RoBERTa Tagalog, and multilingual transfer with XLM-RoBERTa and Multilingual BERT; (5) Entity disambiguation: Evaluating multi-task joint training with POS tagging and contextual RoBERTa fine-tuning to resolve ambiguous Organization and Location mentions; (6) Cross-dataset evaluation: Bidirectional cross-domain transfer evaluation against WikiANN and manual re-annotation of WikiANN test samples; (7) Zero-shot LLM evaluation: Prompting commercial (GPT-4, Claude 2, Cohere Command) and open-source (Falcon-40B, LLaMA-2, Dolly, OpenLLaMA) LLMs.
datasets: TLUNIFIED-NER - Gold-standard Tagalog Named Entity Recognition dataset containing ~7.8k documents (6,700 train, 545 dev, 558 test; 208,247 tokens) annotated across Person (8,024 spans), Organization (6,706 spans), and Location (10,753 spans; total 25,483 entity spans) sourced from TLUnified news articles (2009-2020)
WikiANN Tagalog - Silver-standard dataset containing 100 train and 100 test documents (alongside a newly re-annotated gold test set) used for cross-dataset evaluation

supervised_and_transfer_benchmarks.baseline_train_from_scratch_f1: Evaluated on test set across 3 trials
supervised_and_transfer_benchmarks.static_fasttext_byte_cloze_f1: Evaluated on test set across 3 trials
supervised_and_transfer_benchmarks.monolingual_roberta_tagalog_f1: Highest performing contextual model with substantial error reduction on ORG and LOC mentions

llm_zero_shot_benchmarks.observation: Supervised transition-based models consistently outperform zero-shot prompting across all tested LLMs

key_findings: Iterative gold-standard annotation by native Tagalog speakers achieves high inter-annotator agreement (Cohen's kappa of 0.81 for non-null tokens and 0.83 ignoring 'O' labels; reference F1 of 0.89), validating the quality of the ~7.8k document TLUNIFIED-NER corpus.

Fine-tuning monolingual contextual embeddings (RoBERTa Tagalog) achieves superior NER performance and substantial relative error reduction on ambiguous Organization and Location entities compared to static fastText vectors and train-from-scratch baselines.

Supervised transition-based models fine-tuned on TLUNIFIED-NER consistently outperform zero-shot large language model prompting across both open-source (Falcon-40B, LLaMA-2, Dolly, OpenLLaMA) and commercial LLMs (GPT-4, Claude 2, Cohere Command).

Models trained on TLUNIFIED-NER achieve stronger cross-dataset generalization than silver-standard WikiANN models, and manual re-annotation confirms pervasive annotation errors and text fragment issues in the Tagalog portion of WikiANN.
Joint multi-task training of POS tagging with transition-based NER via shared representation weights improves entity disambiguation when entity mentions exhibit lexical and semantic category overlap.

Information-theoretic distinctiveness metrics reveal that Person and Location entities exhibit higher boundary distinctiveness than Organization entities, explaining lower baseline model performance on organization span boundaries.
scope_and_delimitations: Restricted source text domain strictly to news reports published between 2009 and early 2020 from Metro Manila news outlets in the TLUnified pretraining corpus.
Delimited entity categories to three flat CoNLL-style entity classes (Person, Organization, Location), deliberately excluding the Miscellaneous (MISC) tag to reduce annotator ambiguity.
Target language delimited exclusively to Tagalog / Filipino, excluding non-standard dialects, Tagalog-English code-switching, and other regional Philippine languages.
Classifier architectures delimited to spaCy transition-based parsers with maxout CNNs and zero-shot LLM prompts, excluding CRFs and BiLSTM sequence taggers.

limitations.verbatim_excerpt: The TLUNIFIED-NER corpora is comprised mostly by news reports. Although the texts demonstrate the standard usage of Tagalog, its domain is limited. In addition, we only trained a transitionbased parser model for our NER classifier. In the future, we plan to extend these benchmarks and include CRFs or other tools such as Stanford Stanza.
limitations.summary: The TLUNIFIED-NER corpus is restricted primarily to the formal news domain, leaving conversational, social media, and informal Tagalog varieties unrepresented. Furthermore, benchmark evaluations are restricted to spaCy's transition-based parsing architecture without exploring sequence labeling architectures like Conditional Random Fields (CRFs) or tools like Stanford Stanza, and the entity schema excludes the miscellaneous (MISC) category and overlapping or nested entity spans.

generalizability_gap: The dataset focuses exclusively on formal news domain Tagalog from Metro Manila news outlets (2009-2020), leaving informal Tagalog, code-switched Taglish (Tagalog-English), regional dialects, and other major Philippine languages (such as Cebuano, Ilocano, and Hiligaynon) unexamined.
methodological_gap: The empirical benchmarks rely primarily on spaCy transition-based parsers with maxout CNNs, leaving Conditional Random Fields (CRFs), BiLSTM-CRF sequence labelers, and token-level transformer classifiers unbenchmarked; zero-shot LLM evaluations were conducted using simple static prompt templates without exploring advanced prompting frameworks (such as PromptNER or few-shot chain-of-thought).
future_work: Extending the NER annotation schema to fine-grained, hierarchical, and overlapping/nested entity types similar to the ACE project.
Expanding gold-standard NER dataset development to other major Philippine languages (such as Cebuano, Ilocano, and Hiligaynon).
Benchmarking additional sequence modeling architectures including Conditional Random Fields (CRFs) and Stanford Stanza.
Exploring advanced prompting strategies such as PromptNER and few-shot chain-of-thought prompting for multilingual large language models.
